gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-tc: Every stroke of Vast Shadow is cut to a single width, giving it a vintage, eye-catching look. Noto Sans TC takes over below with large open curves, and it likes a body size a touch generous.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Vintage and eye-catching, Vast Shadow bends its letters like tubing of one gauge throughout. And Noto Sans Telugu, a plain sans with a high midline, keeps its counters connected to the outside.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-thai: Noto Sans Thai reads friendly and rounded, its lowercase swollen like inflated glass beads. Vast Shadow sits above it in a single monoline stroke, so paragraphs below feel soft and unhurried next to that vintage heading.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-thai-looped: Clean and professional in the text, this pairing sets tall, bold-looking lowercase beneath a heading with no swelling where curves meet stems. Vast Shadow stays crisp; Noto Sans Thai Looped reads steadily.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-tifinagh: Vast Shadow draws strokes like thread stitched along a path, a vintage show-off with plenty of room around each letter. Noto Sans Tifinagh does the opposite job, filling lines with rounded, inviting sans-serif bowls made for sustained reading.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Noto Sans Tirhuta reads contemporary and clean, with a dominant x-height and terminals cut back to leave big gaps. Yet Vast Shadow supplies the glow, its neon-tube letters holding one line thickness from end to end.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Noto Sans Ugaritic stays approachable and clean, with a minimal gap between x-height and cap height and open mouths like unjoined chalk arcs. Vast Shadow adds the vintage flourish.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-vai: Bold vintage letters, then a friendly block of text. Noto Sans Vai makes words read as solid blocks rather than skylines, with generous space between curve ends and the stem, so a longer passage moves along smoothly.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Noto Sans Vithkuqi reads clean and modern, with open throats on its a, c, e and s. Vast Shadow does the showy work with a monoline stroke from start to finish, while the sans handles the quiet, steady reading.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Noto Sans Wancho has a hulking lowercase, like thick chalk pressed hard, and an e with a wide gap at its terminal. And Vast Shadow keeps its arms and legs at constant width, so a modest body size is plenty.
